chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father, from Ali (peace be upon him): Regarding

a man who has a debt due from another man, and he demands it from him, but the debtor has no means to pay it. So the creditor says to him, 'It is with you as a mudarabah (profit-sharing partnership).' He (the Imam) said, 'It is not valid until he takes possession of it from him.'
ai.seo_question: Is it valid to convert a debt into a mudarabah partnership if the debtor has no money to pay?
ai.summary: This ruling from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies that merely declaring a debt as capital for a mudarabah is insufficient; the creditor must physically take possession (qabd) of the assets to establish a valid partnership, thereby preventing the concealment of insolvency. This principle underscores the Shia juristic emphasis on actual transfer of ownership and risk in commercial contracts, ensuring that the creditor assumes true entrepreneurial risk rather than merely holding a secured claim.
